root_idea.summary: The root centers on holding, restraining, or firmly grasping something, whether physically, morally, or intellectually.
root_idea.development: Its meanings extend from binding and confinement to the mental restraint that enables understanding, reflection, and discernment; related developments include refuge, bloodwit, and things held together or made secure.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The group is a Quran-attested Form I verb and is presented under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To understand or comprehend something; to know what was previously unclear.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively with an object or pronominal reference. In Quranic usage, the verb concerns acquired understanding rather than merely possessing an innate mental faculty.

senses.definition: To use understanding in reflection, reasoning, and discernment.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of drawing understanding from signs, teachings, parables, and events, especially in contexts contrasting sound reasoning with heedlessness or rejection. This is an exercise of intellect, not a separate noun meaning of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or fasten, especially to tie a camel’s foreleg with an عِقَال; hence, to hold back or restrain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The physical use concerns binding an animal; the extended use concerns restraining a person from an aim or want.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic use derived from the binding of a woman’s limbs; it is a Classical Arabic idiom, not a Quranic sense of the supplied verb group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay or provide the bloodwit for a slain person; عَقَلَ عَنْهُ means to pay it on someone’s behalf, and عَقَلَ لَهُ دَمَ فُلَانٍ to relinquish retaliation in exchange for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A legal and customary use involving blood compensation and the parties responsible for it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set a person up on one leg by raising or positioning it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical action derived from the binding or raising of a limb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of medicine, to bind or confine the bowels; to act as an astringent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the belly when it becomes confined or stops running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect or exact the poor-rate of a people or group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction عَقَلَ عَلَى القَوْمِ is used for collecting their obligatory levy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw an opponent in wrestling by twisting one’s leg around or against his leg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized wrestling technique involving the legs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, to comb her hair, especially in a specified manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence attests the expression as a conventional use; the reference to a woman belongs to the expression itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intelligent or to become possessed of understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an intransitive state or change-of-state use, distinct from the transitive sense ‘to understand a thing.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mountain goat or gazelle, to make itself inaccessible in a mountain; also, to betake oneself to someone or somewhere for refuge, protection, shelter, or lodging.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal use describes seeking safety in elevated terrain; the broader construction عَقَلَ إِلَيْهِ means to seek refuge or lodging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of shade, to decline, contract, or nearly disappear at midday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the shortening of shade as the sun rises high.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thorny plant upon which camels graze, identified with the prickly hedysarum or alhagi.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used for the plant in Egyptian and related botanical contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to have a twisting, excessive spreading, or knocking together of the hind legs or knees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical defect of an animal’s hind limbs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported phrase interpreted as ‘dismiss doubt from yourself.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence records the phrase as disputed and says that it was considered an error for مَا أَغْفَلَهُ; it is therefore not a secure productive meaning of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, not to receive fecundation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or tropical expression recorded in Classical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone intelligent or make him possess understanding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form II use, distinct from the intransitive state of being intelligent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a grapevine, to put forth its first, sour grapes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical use referring to grapes in their early sour state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be treated as equal in bloodwit, or to exchange bloodwit liability on an equal basis up to a specified threshold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested legal formulation concerns the comparative bloodwits of a woman and a man up to one-third of the woman’s full bloodwit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compete with someone in intelligence and surpass him in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form III use concerning comparison or rivalry in understanding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To owe what is termed an عِقَال, namely a year’s poor-rate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV use in the terminology of obligatory levies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a people, to enter the condition in which the shade has declined and contracted at midday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV intransitive use derived from the specialized shade sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find or judge someone to be intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV evaluative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place or interlace one’s hands so that another person can use them as a step to mount a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression تَعَقَّلْ لِي بِكَفَّيْكَ; the meaning is a physical supporting arrangement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To conceive something in the mind, especially abstractly; to regard it as intelligible or conceivable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A philosophical or technical use, as in saying that something is not conceivable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recover one’s understanding or to exert oneself to acquire intelligence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive use can describe restoration of understanding or deliberate cultivation of it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a hunted animal, to become caught or stuck in a net or similar trap.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence describes this as a coined, nonstandard hunting term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay or share bloodwits among themselves jointly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or collective legal use concerning mutual payment of blood compensation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect or pretend to possess intelligence without actually possessing it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or behavioral use describing a display of عقل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be withheld, restrained, or confined; of the tongue, to be prevented from speaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive form اُعْتُقِلَ and the intransitive Form VIII construction describe confinement or inability to speak.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place or fold a limb, spear, saddle part, or similar object between the leg and another support.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes putting a ewe’s hind legs between one’s thigh and shin while milking, carrying a spear beneath the thigh, and folding the leg onto a saddle support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To insert one leather strip beneath another while sewing a skin, strengthening it and preventing water from passing through.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical leatherworking use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or receive the bloodwit for someone’s blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction اِعْتَقَلَ مِنْ دَمِ فُلَانٍ or مِنْ طَائِلَتِهِ concerns receiving the compensation owed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To count, account, or esteem someone as intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X evaluative use derived from عاقل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bloodwit or a mulct for bloodshed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive use of the verbal noun; the plural is مَعَاقِلُ. The term is explained through the traditional binding of camels collected as compensation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intelligence, understanding, intellect, mind, reason, or knowledge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Can denote the faculty prepared to receive knowledge or the understanding and knowledge acquired through it; it may also mean the capacity to distinguish sound from unsound or better from worse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fortress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is explicitly reported as doubtful and is cross-referred to مَعْقِلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of red or figured cloth used to cover a camel vehicle or made as a patterned textile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A material-culture term with several recorded descriptions of the cloth’s color and pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bond like an عِقَال or a shackle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete restraint or fastening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impediment or obstruction, including an impediment attributed to enchantment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The magical use occurs in the expression بِهِ عُقْلَةٌ مِنَ السِّحْرِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wrestling technique consisting of twisting one’s leg with another’s.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal designation for the action described under عَقَلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A twisting or obstruction of the tongue when one wants to speak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A speech-related physical or expressive impediment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In geomancers’ terminology, a configuration consisting of a unit, a pair, and a unit, represented by two parallel bars with a small circle above and below.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized technical meaning, also called ثِقَافٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intellectual; relating to the intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attributive adjective derived from عَقْلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rope used to bind a camel’s foreleg to its arm, with the two folded together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is عُقُلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A year’s poor-rate or obligatory levy, especially a levy consisting of camels, sheep, or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to the livestock levy itself, its value, or, in some interpretations, the rope given with the livestock.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A young she-camel of the kind called قَلُوص.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological or pastoral noun distinct from the rope and levy senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A high-ranking man whose ransom, if captured, is paid in hundreds of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression concerning ransom value.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicine that binds, confines, or astringes the bowels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for an astringent medicine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A noble or highly esteemed woman; by extension, the finest or most excellent member or example of a kind, including a chief or an excellent camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary social use concerns a woman of generous lineage who is kept in seclusion and held in high esteem; the extended use applies to substantial or ideal things.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pearl, especially a large, clear, or choice pearl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional designation of a prized pearl as the finest treasure of the sea.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hardy, excellent, highly esteemed camel of Najd.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used attributively with camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease or slight lameness affecting an animal’s legs, especially the hind legs, causing it to limp intermittently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression دَاءٌ ذُو عُقَّالٍ describes a disease from which recovery does not occur.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The three herbs that remain after cutting, identified as السعدانة, الحُلَّب, and القُطْبَة.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral and botanical collective term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The raised or supported portions of a grapevine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression for vine branches trained on a trellis or similar support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Grapes in their first, sour state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical noun for unripe or early sour grapes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An idiomatic expression equated with شَغْزَبَ and شَغْرَبَ, denoting a named physical twisting or struggling action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence preserves the synonymic equation but does not resolve the precise English nuance of the expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A payer of bloodwit; collectively, the paternal relatives or allied group responsible for paying compensation for an accidental killing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective عَاقِلَة may include paternal male relatives, registered members of a group, or another legally recognized body responsible for the payment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possessing intelligence or understanding; rational or intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman; the evidence also records a more intensive form and several plural patterns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain goat or gazelle that protects itself in an inaccessible mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A zoological epithet derived from the animal’s seeking refuge in elevated terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female comber of the hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational or agent noun distinct from the bloodwit collective and the adjective meaning intelligent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bent portion or place of bending in a river, valley, or sand; an angle or winding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural عَوَاقِيلُ is used for bends or angles, especially in valleys.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main or central part of the sea, or its waves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nautical or topographical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land in which one cannot readily find the right way because of its many windings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical description based on winding or confusing terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The confused, complicated, or dubious aspects of affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural expression derived from winding or entangled terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evil actions or things that cause trouble; hence, a person who produces such complications.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression إِنَّهُ لَذُو عَوَاقِيلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great heap or extended hill of intermingled, accumulated sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural includes عَقَاقِلُ and عَقَاقِيلُ; the form reflects massing, winding, or interweaving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great or wide valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A topographical noun with the same plural patterns as the sand sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The intestines or related internal portion of a ضَبّ, a desert lizard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also associated with the animal’s كُشْيَة; the expression urging one to feed a brother from it is proverbial and variably interpreted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drinking cup or bowl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, having the hind-leg twisting or defect called عَقَلٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form عَقْلَاءُ is applied to a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More intelligent or most intelligent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjective related to عَاقِلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of refuge, protection, preservation, shelter, or lodging; a fortress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used literally of a refuge or stronghold and metaphorically of a person who is the refuge of his people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where camels are bound with an عِقَال.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete pastoral use underlying the broader refuge sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place that retains rainwater.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is tentatively implied in the cited lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A variety of dates, or fresh ripe dates, associated with al-Basrah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained as a nisbah to the personal name مَعْقِل بن يسار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bound with the rope called عِقَال; of a she-camel, bound in that manner during covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مُعَقَّلَاتٌ is also applied metaphorically to women in a similar sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perceived by the intellect, intelligible, or approved as reasonable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical passive-participial adjective used especially for knowledge or propositions that are intellectually conceived rather than simply transmitted; the plural مَعْقُولَاتٌ has the same branch of meaning.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Tentative lexical implication is preserved in the target usage conditions.
Grammatical identification as a passive participle.
Plural form with the same lexical branch.

cautions: The Quran form group is represented by the normalized citation form عَقَلَ, although the QAC lemma identity and most occurrences are imperfect forms.

Lane records a few doubtful, disputed, or technically specialized items, including the fortress sense of عَقْلٌ, the rain-retaining-place sense of مَعْقُلَةٌ, and the phrase مَا أَعْقِلُهُ عَنْكَ; their uncertainty is stated locally rather than treated as ordinary core meanings.
The Classical noun عَقْلٌ meaning intellect is not presented as a separate Quranic form because the supplied QAC root contains only the Form I verb.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The exact English nuance of the idiom العِقِّيلَى is unresolved in the packet; it is retained as an idiomatic item through Lane’s explicit equation with شَغْزَبَ and شَغْرَبَ.
The reported meaning of مَا أَعْقِلُهُ عَنْكَ is disputed in the Lane passage and may reflect an error for مَا أَغْفَلَهُ.
